subject: System Design
title: GitLab Deletes Its Own Database
description: A micro-lesson that makes GitLab Deletes Its Own Database usable.

hook.text: On January 31, 2017, a GitLab engineer accidentally ran a delete command on the production database.

buildup.text: They were troubleshooting a replication issue and typed the command in the wrong terminal window.

discovery.text: 300 GB of production data was deleted. The team scrambled to restore from backups.

twist.text: Five different backup methods had all failed silently. The only working backup was a 6-hour-old snapshot.

climax.text: GitLab live-streamed the recovery on YouTube with full transparency. They lost 6 hours of user data.

punchline.text: Untested backups are not backups at all.

quiz.question: What made GitLab's database deletion so damaging?
options: Five backup methods had all failed silently
They didn't have any backup system
